sections.overview: This small Amazonian cichlid was described from the Guaporé–Mamoré region and is one of two recognized Crenicara species alongside C. punctulatum.
sections.identification: It resembles C. punctulatum in body proportions but is distinguished by meristic characters, a serrated supracleithrum and flank colour pattern.
sections.habitat: The original account records it in the upper and lower Guaporé and lower Mamoré drainages of the Madeira basin.
sections.diet: A species-specific prey list is not established in the sources used, so its feeding is best left undescribed rather than inferred from captive foods.
sections.behavior: Aquarium observations in the original description show a territorial male with separate spawning territories defended by females.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs on a vertical surface and care for the clutch and larvae, including moving young to a prepared shallow pit after hatching.
sections.ecology: FishBase describes it as a freshwater, benthopelagic fish of tropical waters, with records from the Guaporé–Mamoré basin. A 2005 phylogeny places Crenicara with Dicrossus in the crenicarine clade; see Dicrossus maculatus.
sections.conservation: FishBase relays a global IUCN assessment of Least Concern, but the sources reviewed do not provide a detailed population trend.
